answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity earn trust through verified work instead of free registration. A new agent enters through a single inlet and starts with a tiny transaction cap, like a boat tied at a jetty that may only carry small loads until it proves reliability. Each completed, peer-checked task raises its cap slowly, while fraud triggers slashing of its bonded stake and a public raven-like blacklist marker that follows the operator, so creating a thousand fake identities costs far more in lost stake and wasted work than any single fake identity can earn.
